Financial Case: ROI, Payback, Risk-Adjusted NPV, and Funding Requirements (2026–2031)
The financial analysis for the proposed asset purchase presents three headline metrics that underpin the
business case. Base-case ROI is 38% over five years (2026–2030). Simple payback period is 2.6 years
from the 2026-03-31 commissioning date. Risk-adjusted NPV is $3.2M at a 10.5% discount rate. These
outcomes reflect modeled cash flows, operating cost reductions, and capital allowances incorporated in
the 2026 budget submission. Senior finance and operations reviewed sensitivities and agreed that these
base assumptions are realistic for Board-level approval.
Detailed cash-flow projections separate 2026 commissioning costs from recurring benefits across the
2026–2031 horizon. Capital expenditure of $6.8M is scheduled in Q1 2026 with depreciation and tax
treatment as outlined in the corporate capital policy. Expected annual operating cost reduction averages
9.4% versus the legacy line, and incremental gross margin improvement through higher throughput is
modeled at approx. $1.1M per annum from 2027. Forecasts assume normal seasonality, with sensitivity
scenarios adjusting benefits by ±20% to stress-test payback and ROI. Currency exposure is hedged per
policy.
Risk analysis applied probability-weighted scenarios to produce a conservative valuation consistent with
Board expectations. Scenario A (base operations) and Scenario B (lower throughput) were weighted 0.7
and 0.3 respectively to reflect execution risk, supply chain volatility, and demand sensitivity. Stress testing
increased the discount to 12.5% in downside cases, reducing value but preserving positivity under base
assumptions. Recommended governance actions include quarterly variance reporting, contingency
triggers, and revised KPI thresholds tied to incentive payments. An independent review will be completed
prior to first draw.
Funding requirements total $6.8M capex with an additional $0.6M allowance for commissioning and
contingency across 2026–2027. Proposed funding mix: 1. internal cash of $2.5M, 2. a three-year term loan
of $3.0M at market rates, and 3. vendor-supplied equipment financing of $1.9M. Draw schedule aligns with

the 2026-03-31 commissioning date and milestone payments. The request to Treasury seeks approval for
the structured financing, covenant terms, and a standby facility to preserve liquidity through the payback
horizon. Board approval is requested at the May 2026 committee.

Investment Rationale and Operational Impact for the Dayton Packaging Line Upgrade
The proposed asset purchase of a new high-efficiency packaging line for the Dayton, OH plant, at a total
installed cost of $8.6M, addresses immediate capacity constraints and aligns with corporate production
targets. Increasing packaging acpacity from 120 units/min to 180 units/min provides a 50% uplift in
throughput, enabling higher order fulfillment, reduced lead times, and optimized lfoor utilization. This
investment supports peak season demand and long-term volume growth at the plant effectively.
Commissioning is scheduled for 2026-03-31 with structured qualification, line integration, and vendor-led
acceptance testing; full run-rate is targeted for 2026-07-01. The phased ramp plan includes controlled
shifts for validation, a 4-week piolt period to validate throughput and OEE, and contingency resources to
limit planned downtime to under 72 hours per mechanical integration phase. Detailed changeover
protocols and cross-functional training will minimize customer-impacting interruptions during the transition
and support rapid defect resolution effectively.
Operational impacts extend to staffing, maintenance, and supplier coordination; a targeted training
program of 80 operator-hours and 40 maintenance-hours will be completed before 2026-07-01 to certify
line operators and significantly rdeuce startup defects. The asset includes predictive-maintenance sensors
with vendor SLA for sapre parts delivery within 72 hours and a 24-month warrnaty. Quality controls will
tighten packaging tolerances, reducing rework and customer claims, while energy-efficient motors are
expected to lower energy intensity.
